introduction: “How can I succeed unless Thou assist me with the breath of the Holy Spirit?” The guide answers with a single promise made a hundred ways: whoever arises to teach is helped, with words, with courage, with unseen hosts, with harvests beyond what was sown; and the teacher is only a reed through which another breath passes. Moses at the bush and Jeremiah with fire in his bones are the old pattern of the unwilling or unable speaker who is given a mouth. Jesus tells his envoys to take no thought what to say; Paul says his sufficiency is of God, that he planted and God gave the increase; the Qur’an tells its Prophet, “thou threwest not when thou didst throw”; Elisha’s servant sees the hills full of chariots of fire; Tagore and Rumi both take the reed for their image. Scripture is also wary of the promise. Jeremiah hears of prophets who ran unsent; the seventy are told not to rejoice in their success; the psalm about angels is quoted by the tempter; servants who have done everything are to call themselves unprofitable; and some who prophesied in the Name are not known.
questions: Moses is promised a mouth and the disciples are told to take no thought what they shall speak; Peter asks for a reason ready. How do readings 13 and 14 hold inspiration and preparation together?
Gamaliel waits to see whether a work comes to nought; the psalmist is troubled by the prosperity of the wicked. What do the readings count as the “signs” of a confirmed cause?
Jeremiah speaks of prophets who ran though they were not sent. What, in the readings on purity, detachment and the reed, guards against that?
The seventy are told to rejoice that their names are written in heaven, not that spirits obey them. How should the many promises of reward and victory in this guide be held?
“Thou threwest not when thou didst throw.” If it is the Spirit that confirms, what exactly is left for the teacher to do, and why do the readings insist it be done?

outside.why: “How can I succeed unless Thou assist me?” Moses at the bush pleads that he is slow of speech, and is answered: I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.
Paul’s own account of his fitness: not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God.
“Every soul who teaches is confirmed.” The commission at the end of Matthew carries the same promise: go, teach all nations; and, lo, I am with you alway.
“Deliver the Cause of thy Lord to all who are in the heavens and on earth.” Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.
“Of all the gifts of God the greatest is the gift of teaching.” Proverbs: he that winneth souls is wise.
The Prophet to ‘Alí before Khaybar: if one man is guided through you, it is better for you than the red camels, the most prized wealth of Arabia.
Teaching is to be pursued under all conditions. Paul: necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel.
A good intention will draw confirmations. The Gospel’s test looks the other way round, at what comes of the work: by their fruits ye shall know them. Is the intention or the fruit the surer sign?
“One must never consider one’s own feebleness.” My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise, and the weak things to confound the mighty, that no flesh should glory in his presence.
Those who do not spread the message “fail to remember God befittingly”. Jeremiah tried silence: his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I could not stay.
Teaching succeeds by the Spirit, “not by any fund of knowledge”. Socrates tells the reciter Ion that he speaks of Homer not by art but by a divinity moving him, as the magnet moves iron rings.
Peter still asks believers to be ready with a reason for their hope. If the Spirit does the work, why study the proofs? The next reading already answers; how?
“He will inspire thee with words of truth.” Take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.
That the breaths of the Holy Spirit may loosen tongues. They were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak as the Spirit gave them utterance.
Before speaking, turn and ask. O Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall shew forth thy praise.
“Speak out with great courage.” When they had prayed, the place was shaken, and they spake the word of God with boldness.
Turn toward the Kingdom, and with a detached heart begin. Milton begins his poem the same way: and chiefly Thou, O Spirit, instruct me, for Thou know’st.
The Spirit will aid, “provided no doubts obtain in your hearts”. Let him ask in faith, nothing wavering: for he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea.
Speak of what “ye have witnessed with your own eyes”. The Samaritans: we have heard him ourselves, and know.
Souls with capacity “become attracted through a single word”. Lydia heard Paul once: whose heart the Lord opened.
“When a Cause is confirmed it is evident … from its signs.” Gamaliel’s test: if this work be of men, it will come to nought; but if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it.
The psalmist nearly lost his footing when he saw the prosperity of the wicked. Growth and success are claimed by many causes. What kind of fruit is the reading’s evidence?
A tree planted that will be laden with fruit. A sower went forth to sow, and some seed fell on good ground and brought forth an hundredfold.
“This pure seed that thou hast sown shall yield many, many harvests.” In the morning sow thy seed: thou knowest not whether shall prosper.
A seed in fertile soil bears a hundredfold. The Qur’an’s likeness: a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains.
“Now is the time” for sowing. Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.
No one is commanded by name; “whosoever arises” finds the doors open. Whom shall I send? Here am I; send me.
Jeremiah hears God complain of volunteers: I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran. What distinguishes arising from running unsent?
“Whatever has been sown shall be reaped.” Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.
The more you advance, the more confirmations, “to such a degree that you yourselves will be astonished”. Prove me now herewith, if I will not open you the windows of heaven.
“The friends must count time as precious.” Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Make the sightless see and awaken the heedless. I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.
Confirmations encompass the teachers and cease when teaching stops. The Qur’an: if ye help God, He will help you and will make your foothold firm.
“No soul will succeed except the teacher.” The Preacher: the race is not to the swift, nor yet favour to men of skill. What does success mean in this reading?
“You will become eloquent. Your tongue will be loosed.” I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay.
Blessed are those who arise to teach. How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings.
Their heads “crowned with the diadem of everlasting sovereignty”. They that turn many to righteousness shall shine as the stars for ever and ever.
The seventy return elated at their success and are told: in this rejoice not, but rather rejoice because your names are written in heaven. What is a teacher to do with the promise of crowns?
A roll of the provinces of Canada. Ye shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
One of them turning to a region overcomes it. David to Goliath: the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s.

“The triumphant hosts of the Celestial Concourse … stand ready.” Elisha’s servant has his eyes opened and sees the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire: they that be with us are more than they that be with them.
The hosts await those who charge forth. The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him.
“You should pray for them” that they may be able to promote the Word. Epaphras, always labouring fervently for you in prayers.
Arise “in perfect unity” to teach. That they all may be one; that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.
The Feast draws down confirmations. They continued in fellowship, in breaking of bread, and in prayers; and the Lord added to the church daily.
“To awaken spiritual love in others is to attain peace and joy for yourself.” He that watereth shall be watered also himself.
“He, verily, aideth him who aideth Him.” If God helpeth you none can overcome you, and if He withdraw His help from you, who is there who can help you?
“Be not dismayed … when the day-star of My beauty is set.” It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come.
Arise to further the Cause. Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven?
He “turned the rocky ground into a level highway”. Every valley shall be exalted, and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain.
“We behold you … and shall aid whosoever will arise.” Fear thou not; for I am with thee: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee.
Invisible hosts, armies of inspiration. Seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses.
Every soul who arises will be confirmed. If God be for us, who can be against us?
“Let thy heart be at ease and have no fear.” The Lord to Paul by night at Corinth: be not afraid, but speak; for I am with thee, and I have much people in this city.
“My God chooses whomsoever He willeth.” I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious.
If the friends knew what is destined for them. Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.
So much is said of rewards. Jesus: when ye shall have done all, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do. Can one hope for the reward and say this too?
“The father flieth from his son.” I am come to set a man at variance against his father; a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.
The source of courage is promoting the Word. God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Let not the strong of the earth rob you of strength. Peter before the council: we ought to obey God rather than men.
Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.
“The teacher is the reed.” Tagore: this little flute of a reed thou hast carried over hills and dales, and hast breathed through it melodies eternally new.
The individual must become a reed. Rumi’s reed speaks for itself: hearken to the reed-flute, how it complains.
The teacher is only the channel. We have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.
“Do you think it is the teachers who make converts?” I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.
The teacher’s prayer is to be purified so that the Spirit may speak. We preach not ourselves.
“It is not we who do the work.” The Qur’an to the Prophet after Badr: thou threwest not when thou didst throw, but God threw.
The branch cannot bear fruit of itself: without me ye can do nothing.
Look at the Cause, not at ourselves. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
“They that have forsaken their country” to teach. By faith Abraham went out, not knowing whither he went.
A company of angels shall aid whoever arises. The psalm promises angels’ charge too, and the tempter quotes it on the pinnacle of the temple. When does trust in unseen help become tempting God?
The power of the Holy Spirit descends; it remains to arise. Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.

“Teaching is the one Bahá’í service that is confirmed.” On the last day some will say, Have we not prophesied in thy name? and hear, I never knew you. What must accompany teaching for that not to be said?

shortfall: Many of the readings repeat a single promise, that whoever arises to teach will be confirmed, in nearly the same words; companions were chosen for each distinct form of it (the weak made strong, words given in the hour, the seed and the harvest, the unseen hosts, the reed) and not for every repetition.
